epic.title: program(conformance): differential oracle harness — pinned Electron recorder, Keld replayer, comparator, canonical bytes, CI lanes, maturity ladder
epic.body:
## Scope
The measurement machine behind every compat claim: Arm A records Keld-owned fixture apps under the pinned Electron 44.4.5 binary (npm dist shasum recorded; tag → commit 694f45852a0f1726cd23bfd379854de489cccb65) into line-oriented transcripts; Arm B replays the same unmodified fixtures under `@keld/electron`; a Rust comparator in keld-compat normalises declared nondeterministic fields, diffs ordered sequences, and emits one KEL-74 evidence record per cell. The pinned doc sentence is the oracle; the golden transcript is evidence-of-record (observed-only cells cap at BEHAVIOR_MATCH, recorded `unknown` with the oracle id naming the unspecified path).

## Maturity ladder (this is the ladder every family uses)
BEHAVIOR_MATCH (Keld transcript == golden under normalisers, ≥1 OS, legacy_sandbox_off) → CONFORMANCE_PASS (cited doc sentence + Keld-owned test independent of the diff + named negative control + all three OS lanes or explicit ▲) → CORPUS_VERIFIED (same observable matched in a real corpus app through migrate + dev smoke, panel product once a product corpus id is committed, authority profile printed).

## Linear owners consumed
KEL-74 (schema/scorer; shared Manifest/exact-bytes helpers must be promoted out of test-local code), KEL-237 (lifecycle corpus; canonical-bytes rule already live there), KEL-77 (two-arm harness shape; fixture-set digest algorithm §4.3), KEL-81 (CI routing), KEL-78 (authority profile truth), product-corpus owner (none today — DOCUMENTED_COMMITTED_PRODUCT list is empty).

## Design facts fixed by research (two refuters)
- Fixture family: `main.js` (ESM, type:module) + `preload.cjs` (CJS) + `index.html`, markers via synchronous stdout writes; the Electron binary is never committed and never runs in the PR lane.
- Canonical bytes: manifest exact committed bytes (sha256 asserted with a one-byte mutation control — live in the lifecycle corpus test); fixture-set digest per KEL-77 §4.3; each golden is its own immutable blob; the spec must state which digest `artifact.sha256` carries.
- Lanes: PR lane replays committed goldens inside the keld-compat test target on the existing three-OS matrix (offline, deterministic); a weekly recorder lane (TARGET: no scheduled workflow exists) re-records at the same pin to detect oracle nondeterminism and needs its own failure sink or "regression = P1" is unenforced.
- Comparison is strict within one process's sequence space plus explicit causal edges; timing never compared in conformance cells.

refuter_verdicts_batch1.lens: Keld invariants, ownership and reuse (four uniques; default-deny; no Electron-isms in keld-core/keld-ipc; one rule one owner; reuse of KEL-74/77/78/237 owners; measured perf; spec+Linear gate; prior decisions #312/#313/#319/#322/#323/#325 and KEL-127). Verified against <keld repo> at d150a14, Linear (KEL-237/KEL-77/KEL-74 read 2026-10-06), raw Electron v44.4.5 docs/workflow, and one local Bun 1.4.2 probe.

verdicts.reason: The oracle principle is confirmed by three independent owners: crates/keld-compat/AGENTS.md ('Electron documented behavior = oracle. Conformance entry (citing doc/fixture) *before* implementation'), docs/specs/kel77-bun-child-process-differential.md §4.1 ('Rejected: using the Node arm's live output as the oracle — a mirror, not an oracle'), and .agents/testing.md ('Every test MUST use an independent oracle ... upstream behavior'). A pinned recorded transcript is admissible as 'upstream behavior' evidence but cannot be the record's oracle. Two things in the proposed answer are not reuse-clean and must be corrected before it is implemented.
verdicts.evidence: crates/keld-compat/AGENTS.md line 5; kel77 spec §4.1 'Failure' bullet (three states pass/fail/unknown; 'Collapsing unknown into pass would manufacture a compatibility claim'); crates/keld-compat/tests/lifecycle_corpus.rs Manifest/CorpusCell structs are #[serde(deny_unknown_fields)] with fields {operation_id, oracle_id, expected_verdict, test_path, test_name, negative_control, intentional_divergence}; crates/keld-compat/src/evidence.rs parse_verdict accepts only pass|fail|unknown|waived.
verdicts.correction: (1) State the ledger mapping explicitly: an observed-only cell (golden, no doc_blob_oid) is recorded `result: unknown` with oracle.id naming the unspecified path, per KEL-77 §4.1's three-state rule; it is never `pass`. BEHAVIOR_MATCH/CONFORMANCE_PASS/CORPUS_VERIFIED are report vocabulary, not a second verdict set. (2) Do not introduce a new cell shape; extend the live KEL-237 manifest cell with optional {doc_blob_oid, doc_sentence_sha256, golden_sha256, normalizers} after extracting that struct to a shared owner (see extra findings), keeping expected_verdict/test_path/test_name so lifecycle_corpus.rs's execution-admission checks still apply.

verdicts.reason: Both named falsifiers were settled by primary evidence: Electron v44.4.5 docs/tutorial/esm.md states ESM main-process entry is supported since electron@28.0.0 when 'The nearest parent package.json has "type": "module"' or the file ends in .mjs; and a local probe shows Bun 1.4.2 applies tsconfig `paths` to a plain .js `import { app } from "electron"` (resolved to packages/@keld/electron/src/index.ts, process.type=browser, versions.electron=0.0.1, exit 0). Never committing the Electron binary matches docs/architecture/04-electron-compat.md §6 ('separate repo, gitignored fixtures') and the dependency-review gate in ci.yml. The CI router already treats packages/@keld/electron/fixtures as part of the parent package and re-routes keld-compat Rust tests on fixture changes (tools/ci_changes.sh lines 276-300, 645-650), so the proposed fixture placement does not create a skipped-green path.
verdicts.evidence: Probe: <scratchpad>/probe/js-alias/main.js under Bun 1.4.2 printed 'RESOLVED file://<keld repo>/packages/@keld/electron/src/index.ts' and 'TYPE browser VER 0.0.1 function'. esm.md v44.4.5 quotes above. packages/@keld/electron/fixtures/package.json already has "type": "module". tools/ci_changes.sh comments: 'a nested fixture manifest (packages/@keld/electron/fixtures) is part of its parent package's contract' and 'crates/keld-compat spawns the @keld/electron fixtures ... a shim change must still re-run that crate's conformance tests'.
verdicts.correction: Add two constraints the object omits: (a) esm.md: 'ES Modules are loaded asynchronously ... only side effects from the main process entry point's imports will execute before the ready event ... your app may be ready before your code executes' — fixtures MUST register `ready`/lifecycle listeners synchronously at top level before any `await` (the live lifecycle.ts pattern), and the 'APIs before ready' trap cell must be designed knowing `ready` may already have fired in the Electron arm; (b) the Electron arm's npm install (node_modules, lockfile) MUST live outside the fixture directory or KEL-77 §4.3 artifact.sha256 will differ between arms for the same fixture set, firing A3's falsifier spuriously.

verdicts.reason: The three reuse claims check out: lifecycle_corpus.rs asserts denominator.corpus_sha256 == sha256(exact include_bytes! manifest) and flips one byte as a negative control; KEL-77 §4.3 defines the path||0x00||u64_le(len)||bytes digest with the learnings-recorded ('ab','c')/('a','bc') collision control; evidence.rs validates `sha256:<64 hex>` digests and evidence_uri pins, and keld-compat's Cargo.toml carries sha2 as a dev-dependency only. Using the Electron commit (not version string) as oracle revision matches the live record format `electron-v44.3.0@07e46071...`. The rejected alternatives (RFC 8785, hand-rolled hashing) are correctly rejected under AGENTS.md §2/§3.
verdicts.evidence: crates/keld-compat/tests/lifecycle_corpus.rs lifecycle_corpus_denominator_matches_exact_manifest_bytes (mutated[index]=b'E' control); docs/specs/kel77-bun-child-process-differential.md §4.3; docs/agents/learnings.md line 118; crates/keld-compat/Cargo.toml [dev-dependencies] sha2; crates/keld-compat/fixtures/lifecycle-corpus/evidence/macos-aarch64--app-when-ready-host-ready-gate.json oracle.revision.
verdicts.correction: 'Reuse, do not invent' is only true if the code is actually shared. Today both primitives are test-local: the Manifest struct and exact-bytes check live only in crates/keld-compat/tests/lifecycle_corpus.rs, and the §4.3 directory digest is a private `fn corpus_digest(dir: &Path)` at crates/keld-runtime/tests/child_process_differential.rs:288. A second corpus that copies either is the duplicate-policy defect AGENTS.md §3 forbids. The X01 spec MUST name one owner (e.g. a keld-compat test-support module or a cold `keld_compat::corpus` module behind the existing sha2 dev-dependency) and migrate KEL-237/KEL-77 callers to it in the same PR series. Also note the live KEL-237 convention sets artifact.sha256 = the manifest digest, while X01 proposes artifact.sha256 = the fixture-set digest; both are valid per corpus but the manifest must declare which, since score() refuses percent when contributing records disagree on artifact digest.

verdicts.reason: The PR-lane contract is real: ci.yml 'clippy + test' runs on [ubuntu-latest, macos-latest, windows-latest] with oven-sh/setup-bun 1.4.2 on all three, so `cargo test -p keld-compat` can spawn the Bun arm offline; .agents/ci.md requires job-level routing and says 'CI required ... rejects missing, cancelled, failed, or selected-as-skipped evidence' and forbids 'continue-on-error ... retries, skips'; the router fails closed on unknown paths and routes both crates/* and packages/@keld/electron/fixtures changes to the keld-compat lane. The Electron workflow facts are confirmed verbatim (DISPLAY ':99.0', `xvfb-run script/actions/run-tests.sh`, `--enableRerun=3`). Expected-verdict flip detection is already the live pattern (KEL-237's fail cell is a passing test that asserts the divergence).
verdicts.evidence: .github/workflows/ci.yml lines 99-109, 158-160; .agents/ci.md 'Required workflow and routing' and 'Failure preservation'; tools/ci_changes.sh lines 492, 619-650; raw.githubusercontent.com/electron/electron/v44.4.5/.github/workflows/pipeline-segment-electron-test.yml lines quoted; crates/keld-compat/fixtures/lifecycle-corpus/corpus.json cell app.quit.return-contract.
verdicts.correction: The weekly lane is TARGET, not an existing home: the Keld repo has only ci.yml and keldbot.yml, neither with `schedule:`/`workflow_dispatch`, and `CI required` only aggregates PR/push jobs, so a weekly drift failure cannot by itself block merges. The object must (a) label the weekly recorder/corpus-smoke lane as a new workflow (corpus repo per arch 04 §6, or a Keld scheduled workflow landing in its own CI-routing PR per .agents/ci.md), and (b) state that drift findings enter the gate only via a reviewed PR that flips cells to `unknown`/updates goldens+receipts — otherwise 'regression = P1' is enforced only for the Keld arm replay.

verdicts.reason: Every principle cited is confirmed (.agents/testing.md: no sleeps, timeout is only a kill switch, child-process for lifetime with stdout/stderr/exit/signal assertions; AGENTS.md perf decomposition separating clock/statistic; electron_lifecycle.rs LineLog.wait_contains/drain_queued; KEL-72 ▲ for per-listener isolation on the scoreboard). But the decision's own observable contract — a negative-control mutation flips the cell under declared normalizers — cannot be exercised today: there is no comparator, no golden, and the Keld arm has no renderer/preload (no window registry symbol in crates/*/src; arch 01 lists it as keld-core responsibility, TARGET). Whether Electron 44.4.5 main-process ordering is stable enough for strict comparison without normalizers, and whether routing renderer rows through ipcRenderer.send perturbs the order under test, are empirical and unmeasured.
verdicts.evidence: .agents/testing.md 'Cases and test shape' and taxonomy row 'Crash, teardown, restart, or lifetime'; crates/keld-compat/tests/electron_lifecycle.rs LineLog (recv_timeout 8s then panic); grep for WindowRegistry/headless in crates/*/src returns nothing; docs/architecture/01-overview.md line 106.
verdicts.correction: Cheapest settling experiment (no CI, no Keld change): in the scratchpad, run the quit-order fixture under `npx electron@44.4.5 .` 10x on macOS and diff transcripts (A5 prototype 2); then add a renderer that emits markers via ipcRenderer.send and compare main-only vs main+renderer orderings (prototype 3). Until that runs, restrict A5's claim to main-process rows. Also fix a reaping gap carried from the live pattern: LineLog's timeout panics without killing the child (std::process::Child is not killed on drop), so 'Rust test owns and reaps each arm' needs an explicit kill-on-drop guard — critical for the Electron arm, which would otherwise hold the xvfb display.

verdicts.reason: Confirmed against the owners: KEL-77 §4.5 ('authority_profile is deliberately not strict_bun ... would claim the measurement was taken under Keld's zero-ambient-authority profile, which is false'); report.md records legacy_sandbox_off and 'not a product/median-app Electron compatibility percentage'; evidence.rs DOCUMENTED_COMMITTED_PRODUCT_CORPORA is `&[]`, score() omits percent for uncommitted product ids and refuses complete/percent when contributing records disagree on digest/profile/engine (mixed_artifact_identity_refuses_complete_and_percent); the claim shape is formatted exactly as `{passed}/{n} of {panel} corpus {id}@{digest} ({kind})` at evidence.rs:814. Linear confirms KEL-74 Done, KEL-237 In Progress ('do not create a second scoreboard, denominator model ... or compatibility percentage authority').
verdicts.evidence: docs/specs/kel77-bun-child-process-differential.md §4.5; crates/keld-compat/fixtures/lifecycle-corpus/report.md; crates/keld-compat/src/evidence.rs lines 814-817, 973-980, 1414-1429; Linear KEL-74/KEL-237 descriptions read 2026-10-06.
verdicts.correction: The CORPUS_VERIFIED rung ('strict_bun (KEL-78) or explicitly labeled legacy') omits the state `keld dev` is actually in. docs/specs/kel78-strict-profile-sandbox.md defines profile states `unverified | legacy | strict`, says '`unverified` is the live state of macOS, Windows, and Linux on this SHA', '`strict` cannot be reported from documentation', and 'Electron-compat apps do not silently start `legacy`. If they need it, they declare the Keld profile key'. The KEL-74 closed set has no `unverified` value. So a corpus-app run under today's `keld dev` has no honest authority_profile unless the fixture/corpus app carries the explicit Keld `legacy` declaration (then `legacy_sandbox_off` is truthful, matching KEL-127's visibly labeled legacy profile). State that rule and name the vocabulary gap as a KEL-74/KEL-78 reconciliation item rather than assuming strict_bun rows will appear. Also fix the engine string in the manifest per corpus: the object writes `headless-conformance@<commit>` while live records use `headless-lifecycle-conformance@<commit>`; score() refuses percent when contributing records disagree on engine.

extra_findings.finding: Shared-owner gap: the two primitives the object says it 'reuses' are test-local. The manifest struct + exact-bytes digest check exist only inside crates/keld-compat/tests/lifecycle_corpus.rs; the KEL-77 §4.3 directory digest is a private `fn corpus_digest(dir: &Path)` at crates/keld-runtime/tests/child_process_differential.rs:288. A second corpus (X01) cannot call either without copying it, which is the duplicate-policy defect AGENTS.md §3 forbids. The X01 spec must create one owner and migrate KEL-237 and KEL-77 callers to it.
extra_findings.evidence: grep -rn 'fn corpus_digest' crates/ → only crates/keld-runtime/tests/child_process_differential.rs:288; lifecycle_corpus.rs defines Manifest/CorpusCell locally with deny_unknown_fields; crates/keld-compat/src has only evidence.rs (no corpus/manifest module).

extra_findings.finding: The maturity ladder (BEHAVIOR_MATCH → CONFORMANCE_PASS → CORPUS_VERIFIED) has no representation in the only verdict owner. evidence.rs accepts exactly pass|fail|unknown|waived and KEL-237's scope forbids a second scoreboard/percentage authority. Unless the object fixes the mapping (observed-only → `unknown`; doc-cited → `pass`/`fail`; CORPUS_VERIFIED = a distinct product-panel corpus, not a verdict), the ladder becomes a parallel scoring vocabulary.

extra_findings.finding: KEL-78 / KEL-74 vocabulary mismatch blocks honest labeling of any `keld dev` run today: KEL-78 states `unverified` is the live state on all three OS and forbids inferring `legacy` from Electron facade options; the evidence schema has no `unverified` value. Only an explicit Keld `legacy` declaration makes `legacy_sandbox_off` truthful for corpus-app rows.

The object presents the weekly recorder/drift lane as design rather than TARGET and does not name the CI-routing PR (.agents/ci.md: routing lands in its own Linear-scoped PR) or the corpus-repo workflow that would host it.
extra_findings.evidence: ls .github/workflows; grep schedule/workflow_dispatch/cron returns nothing; .agents/ci.md 'CI routing ... lands in its own Linear-scoped PR'.

extra_findings.finding: Electron ESM async-loading changes two trap cells. esm.md v44.4.5: 'only side effects from the main process entry point's imports will execute before the ready event ... your app may be ready before your code executes.' A fixture that registers `ready` listeners after a top-level await will miss `ready` in the Electron arm while Keld's whenReady still resolves; and the 'BrowserWindow before ready' cell may not throw in ESM if `ready` already fired. Fixtures must register listeners synchronously before any await, and the before-ready cell needs a CJS or .mjs-with-synchronous-body design.
extra_findings.evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/electron/electron/v44.4.5/docs/tutorial/esm.md retrieved 2026-10-06; packages/@keld/electron/fixtures/lifecycle.ts registers listeners before `await app.whenReady()`.

extra_findings.finding: @keld/electron exports only `app` (plus isCallError). A plain-ESM fixture with `import { BrowserWindow, ipcMain } from 'electron'` fails at ESM link time in the Keld arm, so every cell in that fixture fails together and lifecycle cells in the same file are masked. Fixtures must be partitioned per family, and a link failure must be recorded as `fail` with a KELD code (not `unknown`, not a skipped fixture).
extra_findings.evidence: packages/@keld/electron/src/index.ts exports {app, isCallError, KeldCallError, default}; research 214 Finding: 'Adding fake named exports just to load unrelated tests would be a false oracle'.

extra_findings.finding: The window-all-closed-during-quit trap is real but its owner is ambiguous and touches keld-core: LifecycleSession tracks only `windows: u32` and `ready: bool` (no quit-in-progress state), so a host-initiated quit that closes windows will emit LastWindowClosed. The fix must be a generic host lifecycle state (quitting) in keld-core, not an Electron-ism; it needs its own spec item naming keld-core as owner, otherwise the facade will paper over it in @keld/electron.
extra_findings.evidence: crates/keld-core/src/lifecycle.rs struct fields lines 35-39 and window_closed() lines 138-149; crates/keld-compat/AGENTS.md 'No Electron-isms in keld-core/keld-ipc'.

extra_findings.finding: Spec + ticket owner for X01 itself is unnamed. KEL-237 is scoped to the existing lifecycle slice ('No new Electron API implementation, no compatibility-surface expansion'); KEL-77 in Linear is the VS Code extension-host showcase lane (the harness *shape* lives in its spec doc, but the issue says 'Extract package-agnostic Bun semantic fixtures into the general runtime suite'); KEL-74 is Done. A differential Electron recorder/comparator is a new feature under AGENTS.md's spec+Linear gate (GitHub issue bridge per briefing) and the object should name that gate as its first blocker.
extra_findings.evidence: Linear KEL-237 Non-goals; Linear KEL-77 title and 'Deliberate showcase boundary'; AGENTS.md 'Features require an approved docs/agents/spec-template.md spec plus Linear'.

extra_findings.finding: Live harness reaping gap inherited by both arms: LineLog.wait_contains panics on an 8s timeout but never kills the spawned child (std::process::Child is not killed on drop), contradicting 'Rust test owns and reaps each arm'. For the Electron arm a leaked process also pins the xvfb display and can serialize later cells.
extra_findings.evidence: crates/keld-compat/tests/electron_lifecycle.rs LineLog::wait_contains and spawn_fixture (no kill-on-drop guard).

extra_findings.finding: Fixture-set digest divergence hazard: if the Electron arm installs `electron@44.4.5` into the fixture directory (node_modules/package-lock), KEL-77 §4.3 artifact.sha256 differs between arms for the same fixtures and A3's 'first falsifier' fires on every run. Install outside the digested tree and record the install path in the receipt.
extra_findings.evidence: kel77 §4.3 digests every file under the corpus directory ordered by relative path.

extra_findings.finding: Pin inconsistency is live, not hypothetical: the committed lifecycle corpus is Electron 44.3.0 @07e46071 while X01 baselines 44.4.5 @694f4585 and the briefing notes 44.5.1 is latest stable. inferences: Electron emits app and window lifecycle events on the browser main thread, so a main-only fixture is expected to be order-stable. Nobody has observed this.
The first BrowserWindow id is probably the same on every fresh process, so a window-id normaliser may be unnecessary, and an unnecessary normaliser can hide a divergence.
Ten identical runs bound the per-run flip rate only below roughly 26% at 95% confidence; thirty bound it below roughly 10%. Ten runs alone is weak evidence of determinism.
A single merged order of main and renderer rows will vary in Electron itself (the X01 semantics refuter's finding), so cross-process comparison needs explicit causal edges.

1. Role
Run one bounded determinism experiment on the pinned Electron binary and report observations. You do not own the harness design, the comparator, any Keld code, any golden file or the decision text.

2. Goal
A receipt stating, for Electron 44.4.5 on macOS arm64, whether the main-process quit-order transcript is identical across repeated runs, and the minimal set of fields that had to be normalised to make it so.

3. Success criteria
- SC1: every arm A and B run exits 0 with a complete transcript ending in the quit row and the process exit code. A killed or incomplete run is reported, never retried silently.
- SC2: verdict DETERMINISTIC only if all 30 arm A and B normalised sequences share one SHA-256. Otherwise NONDETERMINISTIC, listing each distinct sequence, its count and the first differing row pair. State the bound: zero flips in 30 runs bounds the per-run flip rate only below about 10% at 95% confidence.
- SC3: doc cross-check, quoting the app.md sentences in the receipt. In every arm A and B run, before-quit precedes the first window close, will-quit follows the last window closed, quit is last, and window-all-closed is absent. In every arm C run, window-all-closed is present. A violation is a finding, not something to normalise.
- SC4: the normaliser list is minimal. Each entry names one field path and cites the observed raw diff that requires it. A candidate with no observed variance (for example the window id) is listed as not needed.
- SC5: negative controls. Swapping two rows in a copy of one transcript changes its hash; changing one event name changes the hash after normalisation; arm C shows the event arm A asserts absent.
- All evidence is real-OS (macOS arm64). Nothing here is a Keld conformance claim.

4. Prerequisites
- Network access to GitHub releases; about 250 MB free disk; a logged-in GUI session.
- No approval is needed: there are no repo, GitHub or Linear writes.
- Read KEL-237 and its comments first. If an unexpired claim there covers Electron recorder work, stop.

5. Resources
- Fixture directory: package.json with type module and main main.js; main.js (ESM); index.html (static). For arm D only add preload.cjs (CommonJS, require('electron')).
- Register every listener synchronously at top level before any await (esm.md: the app may be ready before the entry point finishes).
- Emit one line per event with fs.writeSync(1, ...): seq (process-local counter), proc, kind, name, args as JSON, plus raw pid, monotonic time, window id and any paths.
- Log: will-finish-launching, ready, browser-window-created, did-finish-load, before-quit, window close, window closed, window-all-closed, will-quit, quit with its exit code.
- Trigger: call app.quit() inside the did-finish-load handler. No timers, no sleeps.
- Electron: download the darwin-arm64 zip, verify its sha256 against the PIN, extract it outside the fixture directory and run the binary directly with the fixture path. Do not use npx (it downloads lazily at record time). Keep ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE unset and record the environment.
- Each run is a child process with stdout, stderr and exit code captured and a 60-second kill switch.
- Arms: A = 10 cold sequential runs on an idle machine. B = 20 runs under CPU contention (one busy process per logical core, started before and stopped after; a perturbation, not a synchronisation aid). C = 10 runs of the control variant that calls win.close() and has a window-all-closed listener that logs and then quits. D (report-only) = 10 runs of arm A plus a renderer that sends two ipcRenderer.send markers which main logs on receipt.
- Normalisation: start with an empty set. Hash the ordered rows (proc, kind, name, args) per run. For each field that differs between runs, add one named normaliser for that exact field path and re-hash. Never normalise event name, kind, order, Error.message or exit code.

6. Delegation
None.

7. Verification
- Electron --version prints v44.4.5 and the zip digest equals the PIN.
- SHA256SUMS over the receipt verifies.
- The per-run hash table and the three negative-control outputs are pasted into RECEIPT.txt.

8. Output
One keld.execution-artifact/v1 JSON with status passed, findings, os-unavailable or hard-failure. Evidence rows: the verdict, the distinct-sequence table, the normaliser list with justifications, the arm C control, the arm D observation (stable or unstable interleave and which rows), machine identity and every command with its exit code. The dispatcher posts the result on gyldlab/keld#411; #419 and #494 consume it.

9. Stop rules
- Zip digest mismatch: stop, hard-failure.
- No GUI session: stop, os-unavailable.
- A run that needs a sleep or a retry to complete: stop and report.
- The same step failing after two attempts: stop and report.
- Any need to edit the keld repo, or to normalise order or event names to reach one hash: stop and report as a finding.
- A claim conflict on KEL-237: stop.

research.summary: Design: a two-arm differential harness shaped like KEL-77 (Rust test owns and reaps each arm; hard failure when a binary is missing; exact arm revision in every record). Arm A (recorder) runs Keld-owned fixture apps under the pinned npm electron@44.4.5 binary (dist shasum 0be094f8e783febba75d591106f5c61c1e511b70; tag v44.4.5 -> commit 694f45852a0f1726cd23bfd379854de489cccb65) and emits a line-oriented transcript (seq, process, event, canonical args, monotonic delta). Arm B (replayer) runs the SAME unmodified fixture files with `electron` resolved to @keld/electron (today: tsconfig paths + `bun` child spawned by crates/keld-compat/tests/electron_lifecycle.rs against keld_core::LifecycleSession; TARGET: `keld dev --headless --smoke`, which is reserved/not live). A Rust comparator in keld-compat normalizes declared nondeterministic fields, diffs ordered sequences, and emits one keld.compat.evidence/v1 record per cell. The golden transcript is evidence-of-record, not the oracle: per AGENTS.md and KEL-77 §4.1 the oracle is the pinned Electron doc sentence (blob at commit 694f4585); a cell with no doc sentence can reach BEHAVIOR_MATCH only. Placement: fixtures in packages/@keld/electron/fixtures/<family>/ (plain ESM JS runnable in both arms), goldens/manifest/denominator/evidence/receipts in crates/keld-compat/fixtures/<corpus-id>/ mirroring lifecycle-corpus, comparator tests in crates/keld-compat/tests/, corpus apps (draw.io, Zettlr) in the separate corpus repo (arch 04 §6). CI: PR lane = replay only on the existing 3-OS matrix (deterministic, no Electron download); weekly lane = recorder drift re-run at the same pin (Linux via xvfb-run as Electron's own CI does) + corpus-app smoke; regression P1 = `CI required` fails when any committed cell flips pass->fail/unknown or expected-fail->pass, with no retries, skips, or isCI gating (research 214 Table 4). decisions.question: How are transcripts normalized and compared so that ordering is strict, timing does not create flakes, and 'no sleeps' holds?
decisions.proposed_answer: Transcript row = {seq, proc: main|preload|renderer, kind: event|call|error|exit, name, args: canonical JSON after per-cell normalizers, t_ns: monotonic delta}. Comparison is strict on the ordered (proc, kind, name, normalized args) sequence per cell; t_ns is never compared in conformance cells — it feeds separate budget cells (KEL-90/KEL-129) so clock and statistic stay separate atoms. Normalizers are declared in the manifest per cell (e.g. redact pid, window id, file paths, Error.stack; keep Error.message and code), never inferred. Both arms wait only on observable markers (LineLog pattern) with a timeout that is a kill switch; each arm is a child process whose exit code/signal is part of the transcript (subprocess rule for lifetime). Owner: keld-compat comparator; failure mode: a normalizer so broad it hides a divergence (e.g. redacting the whole args object); observable contract: a negative-control mutation in the Keld arm (swap two event emissions, change an error message) flips the cell to fail; first falsifier: a cell whose normalizers reduce args to `{}` while still scoring pass.
